explanation: Heating sodium hydrogencarbonate (baking soda) breaks it down into sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide — exactly the reaction that makes baked goods rise when baking powder is heated.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Dry white baking soda powder, heated in a test tube.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A drier white residue of sodium carbonate.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs continuous heating to decompose, releasing carbon dioxide and steam.

beaker_view.observation: As the white powder is heated, it fizzes gently and gives off carbon dioxide and steam, leaving a drier white residue behind.
